title: The Signal of the Rust Belt
premise: Hazel Crane, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Meridian-9, has spent three years hiding among the machines, hauling cargo through orbits contested by Earth's collapsing government and the Belt's breakaway colonies. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, Hazel discovers the flicker was a weapon test—and that the massacre it caused at the colony of Vesta Hollow has been erased from every record. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down to permanent silence, Hazel must decode fragments hidden in the station's own maintenance logs, ally with a smuggler crew who become the family he never had, and broadcast proof of the massacre before the loop ends—sacrificing his invisibility, and nearly his life, to give the dead a voice.
about_author: Freya Okafor is a former radio engineer from the Great Lakes region whose fiction blends industrial decay with deep-space wonder. She writes about people who keep the lights on in places everyone else has forgotten.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Weight
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Routine cargo haul through contested orbit is shattered when gravity fails for exactly nine seconds, nearly killing him. The station's AI logs the event as 'atmospheric anomaly.' Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in three years of comfortable invisibility.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He reviews station records and finds the flicker scrubbed from official feeds; his own sensor backups are flagged for deletion. A garbled distress fragment from Vesta Hollow surfaces in an old maintenance log. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Cargo and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Smuggler captain Imani Reyes POV. Her crew docks at Meridian-9 for repairs; she notices Hazel's off-books sensor data and recognizes Vesta Hollow's signature. Beat: wary mutual recognition between two people surviving by staying small.

chapters.title: What the Machines Remember
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He coaxes the station AI, Loomis, into unsealing archived telemetry: nine seconds of gravitational shear aimed at Vesta Hollow—a populated colony of twelve thousand. Beat: horror; the massacre is real and deliberate.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Earth announces its final transmission loop—seventy-two hours of legacy broadcasts before permanent blackout. Whoever controls the last window controls history. Beat: stakes crystallize; time pressure begins.

chapters.title: Twelve Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He finds passenger manifests and personal logs from Vesta Hollow embedded in relay buffers, including a child's voice message. Beat: grief; the abstract becomes unbearably personal.

chapters.title: A Crew Worth Having
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Imani's POV. The smugglers vote to help Hazel despite the bounty on his head. Engineer Dex rigs a broadcast array; medic Suri patches Hazel's radiation burns. Beat: found family forming over shared risk.

chapters.title: The Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Director Vance Okonkwo of Earth's Records Authority. He orders Meridian-9 purged and a hunter ship dispatched. Beat: cold institutional evil; readers see the machinery closing in.

chapters.title: Running Silent
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The crew flees Meridian-9 ahead of the purge, hiding in a derelict mining hulk. Hazel confesses he chose invisibility after losing his own family to a similar cover-up. Beat: vulnerability; trust deepens.

chapters.title: The Hunter
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Cat-and-mouse through debris fields as the hunter ship, Vigilant, closes in. A near-fatal micrometeor run. Beat: escalating tension; the cost of survival made physical.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. Decoding the Vesta Hollow fragments reveals a survivor's beacon still transmitting from the colony ruins—and coordinates. Beat: fragile hope amid despair.

chapters.title: Vesta Hollow
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The crew reaches the ruined colony; frozen corridors, a sealed shelter holding one living survivor, a teenage girl named Wren who recorded everything. Beat: devastation tempered by a single thread of life.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Her account of the nine seconds—watching gravity take her neighbors—interleaved with her mother's final log. Beat: the emotional core; testimony as sacred act.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Dock
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. A trusted fence sells their location to Okonkwo's forces. The Vigilant traps them at Vesta Hollow; Dex is captured covering the escape. Beat: betrayal and sacrifice; family tested.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Okonkwo offers Hazel amnesty and erasure of his past in exchange for silence—survival as complicity. Hazel refuses. Beat: thematic climax of choice; he chooses belonging over safety.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Ensemble, multiple POVs. Countdown to the transmission loop's end; the crew races to hijack a relay buoy powerful enough to reach every colony. Beat: breathless momentum.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Uploading the archive—twelve thousand names, voices, faces—to the broadcast buffer while the station shakes under fire. Beat: determination; love encoded as data.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. Hazel manually holds the damaged antenna alignment through lethal radiation as the loop ends, broadcasting the massacre record system-wide. Beat: peak sacrifice; he collapses as the signal goes out.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Earth goes dark forever—but every colony received the truth. Colonies rise in mourning and revolt; Okonkwo's authority dissolves. Beat: catharsis; the dead are witnessed.

chapters.title: Recovery
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. Hazel survives, burned and changed. The crew nurses him back aboard their patched-together ship. Beat: tenderness; wounds acknowledged, not erased.

chapters.title: No Longer Invisible
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Colonies transmit messages of thanks; Wren formally joins the crew. Hazel deletes his old false identity records himself. Beat: quiet triumph; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Signal Continues
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Hazel's POV. One year later, the crew runs a new relay—voluntary, open, human-tended. Hazel sends a message toward Earth's silent ruins: 'We remember.' Beat: hopeful resolution; belonging chosen, kept, and passed on.
